If you understand this clearly, what fault is there in Deshan’s reviling of Buddhas and cursing of Patriarchs? If you do not understand, then consider Xiangyan burning the wooden Buddha."
The Master’s beard and eyebrows fell out. Thus, it is that fortune and misfortune are summoned by oneself alone. With a shout, he descended from his seat. Miaoxi said:
"As for 'slaying the snake' and 'slaying the cat,' many claim these are the wondrous functions of seizing the opportune moment, or say they are 'great functions' that do not abide by fixed rules.
How could this be the true principle? Those with eyes see the point of landing as soon as [the staff] is raised. If the Great Dharma is not clear, one is merely striking tiles."

When will the divining of the tortoise ever end? Xuefeng asked about the meaning of "beheading the cat. Deshan immediately struck him and drove him out, then called to him again, saying, "Do you understand?
He replied, "I do not understand. Deshan said, "Even with such a grandmotherly heart as mine, you still do not understand.
Yanguan once asked Jueyin about the case of "beheading the cat," to which Jueyin replied, "It must have been Nanquan who did it. When pressed further, Jueyin was unable to respond.
Upon reaching the Sangha Hall, he attained great enlightenment. An ancient said, "From this day forward, I shall no longer doubt the old monk’s tongue"—this is indeed true.
He spoke a verse: "It must be the foremost pivot of Nanquan; Unknowingly and unawares, a blow from the head.

If there were no 'blue and white eyes' facing one another, It would still be like a *gānggā* bird guarding an empty pond. Before he had finished speaking, Yinzong raised his fist and said, "Right at this very moment—"
"At such a time, what would you do? Shang then overturned the meditation seat. Yunyan (Yin) thereupon shouted. Shang said, "It is like drawing a bow after the thief has already fled.

Yuanwu said, "Regarding the story of the cat being killed, 'the place where it is raised' is indeed it. 'The place where it is killed' is acceptable for the moment, but it has nothing to do with the matter.
Even when he does not raise it, it is still all-encompassing. The ancients had those who could settle heaven and earth."
The sword. Now tell me, after all, who was it that slew the cat? It is just like when Nanquan raised [the sword] and said, "If you can speak, I will not kill it.
Suppose at that moment someone had spoken—tell me, would Nanquan have killed it or not? Therefore it is said: "When the true command is being exercised, the ten directions are cut off.
This does not lie in the matter of killing or not killing; if you seek it within the dust of emotions or the realm of intellectual views...

If you were to refute this, you would be failing Nanquan. Rather, look at the edge of the sword as it faces you: there it is, it is not there, and it is neither there nor not there—all are permissible.
Therefore it is said: "When one reaches an impasse, one changes; when one changes, one finds passage. If you do not understand how to change and find passage, you are lost.
"Simply walk upon the words. Nanquan’s raising [of the whisk] in this manner was intended only to cause people to recommend themselves;
each must employ it for themselves and know it for themselves. If you do not understand it in this way, you will ultimately fail to grasp it.

He also said, "When Zhaozhou saved the cat, was he truly like that or not? Zhaozhou then left wearing the shoes on his head. He studied the living word (*huoju*), not the dead word (*siju*). One must...
Carrying one's own household treasure out of the house, one finally beholds the total function and great utility of the ancients.
Nanquan said: "To call it 'suchness' (tathatā) is already a transformation; now you must walk among the heterodox classes. Guizong said:
"Though he performs the actions of a beast, he does not receive the retribution of a beast. The Master said: "Alas, Meng the Eighth! You go about in such a manner. Nanquan asked the Way.
"What is my name? I asked. He replied, "Zongzhi. Baizhang said, "At the place where wisdom does not reach, what is the 'principle' (zong)?
I said, "Be careful not to speak of it. Baizhang said, "If you speak of it, horns will surely grow. Later, when he asked me, "How do you practice at the place where wisdom does not reach?
I withdrew my body and entered the hall. Baizhang returned to his quarters. Yunyan then asked me, "Why did you do that?"
"Not so," I said. "I would say you are quite clever. Yanguan then asked Xuequan, "Why did Zhi not answer?
Xuequan replied, "He was indeed acting among those of a different species. Have you not heard it said: 'Where wisdom does not reach, one must strictly avoid speaking;
one must act directly among those of a different species'? Yanguan did not understand this either. Later, Yanguan asked Yaoshan about it. Yaoshan said, 'What do you think?'"
[Zhao]zhou said, "I understand. [Yaoshan] was silent. Yaoshan laughed loudly. Yanguan asked again, "What is it like to walk among those of different kinds?
Yaoshan said, "I am weary now; let us wait for another time. Yanguan said, "I have come specifically for this reason. Yaoshan said, "Go for now. Yanguan went out.

I heard that Yanguan did not realize [the meaning], so he bit his finger until it bled. When Yanguan returned, [Zhao]zhou asked him, "How was it? Yanguan said, "He would not speak to me. [Zhao]zhou then—
He bowed his head. Zhaozhou said, "I do not ask about the 'different'; what is the 'same'? Nanquan extended both hands toward the ground.
Zhaozhou stepped forward, kicked him over, and shouted "Repentance! Repentance! from inside the hall. Nanquan ordered a monk to ask, "What are you repenting for?

Zhaozhou replied, "I regret not kicking him twice more. Nanquan said to a monk, "There was a fine wind last night. The monk asked, "What kind of wind was it? Nanquan said: [The text here appears to be truncated].
He blew down a pine tree in front of the gate. A monk asked, "What kind of pine is this? He then spoke to another monk, saying, "There was a fine wind last night.
The monk asked, "What kind of wind? Jueyan replied, "It blew down a pine tree in front of the gate. The monk asked, "What kind of pine? Jueyan said, "One gains, one loses.
Furthermore, when Zhaozhou arrived at a hermitage, he asked, "Is there anyone here? Is there anyone here? The master held up his fist. Zhaozhou said:
"The water is too shallow; it is no place to moor a boat. He then went to another hermitage and asked, "Is there anyone here?
Is there anyone here? The master held up his fist. Zhaozhou said, "He can bestow and he can snatch away; he can kill and he can bring to life," and then he prostrated himself.
Yuanwu said, "The tongue of the Way was in Zhaozhou’s mouth, yet he did not know that his own life had already fallen into the hands of another. Had he been able to grasp the supreme net..."
The Master met with the two abbots of the hermitages; this was precisely the moment to distinguish dragons from snakes and separate the monastic from the lay.
It was exactly the time to exert effort. Do you know where Zhaozhou’s point lies? Dingshan said: "In birth-and-death there is no Buddha; if there is no Buddha, then there is no birth-and-death."
Jiashan said, "If there is a Buddha within birth and death, one will not fear birth and death.
[Meishan] certainly did not agree. Later, Jiashan went to see Damei. Jiashan asked, "Which of these is more intimate? Mei said, "One is intimate; the other is distant. Jiashan asked again.
Mei said, "Go for now; come back at another time. The next day, Jiashan asked again. Mei said, "That which is intimate does not ask; that which asks is not intimate."—Ling Xing.
The Lady asked Fubei, "To whom do you entrust this phrase that cannot be grasped even with one's full strength? Fubei said, "Fubei has no superfluous words.
The Lady said, "Before reaching Fubei, it was already a matter for doubt. Fubei said, "If you have another superior point, feel free to bring it forth.
The Lady folded her hands and wept, saying, "Alas! To the midst of heaven, I add further grievance and suffering. Fubei was speechless. The Lady said, "Words..."
Not knowing the biased and the correct, one does not recognize the inverted and the deviant in principle; when one acts for others, calamity arises.

Later, a monk reported this to Nanquan, who said, "Alas, Fubei! He has been broken once by that old woman. When the old woman heard this, she laughed and said, "Master Wang still lacks a certain mechanism.
Master Chengyi asked the old woman, "What is it that Nanquan lacks? The old woman wept and said:
"How pitiable! How tragic! Yixuan was at a complete loss for words. The old woman asked, "Do you understand? Yixuan stood there with palms joined.
The old woman said, "Dead Zen monks are as numerous as hemp and millet. Yixuan reported this to Zhaozhou. Zhaozhou said, "If I had seen him, I would have questioned him until his mouth fell silent.
Yixuan asked, "I do not know how you would have questioned him. Zhaozhou then struck him. Yixuan asked, "Why did you strike me? Zhaozhou said, "Like what?"
"You fellow who would rather die! If you don't strike me now, when do you expect to? Hearing this, the old woman said, "Zhaozhou deserves a blow from my staff.
Later, a monk reported this to Zhaozhou, who wept and said, "How tragic! How painful!

When the old woman heard of this, she joined her palms and said, "Zhaozhou’s eye-sight pierces through the four worlds. Zhaozhou then instructed the monk to ask her, "What is Zhaozhou’s eye? The old woman then—

He raised his fist. The monk reported this to Zhaozhou. Zhaozhou composed a verse, saying: "When the occasion arises, he presents it face-to-face; face-to-face, he acts with the swiftness of the occasion.
I tell you, Laywoman Lingxingpo: why do you weep? What have you lost? The laywoman replied with a verse: "The Master has already understood my cry; now that it is understood, who else could know it?
At that time, under the command of Mahākāśyapa, how many would have lost the opportunity before their eyes? Dana took [the verse].
Dharma Master Danxia burned a wooden Buddha for warmth. The head of the monastery (yuanzhu) scolded him. Danxia brushed away the ashes and said, "I was burning it to retrieve the *śarīra*.

The head of the monastery asked, "How can a wooden Buddha have *śarīra*? Danxia replied, "Since there are none, let us take two more statues and burn them. After that, the head of the monastery’s beard and eyebrows fell out.
Baoning Yong said, "Setting aside the falling of the head of the monastery’s beard and eyebrows for a moment—did Danxia’s eyebrows ever grow back?"
If you see it, you will realize that you have been training alongside the ancient Buddhas; if you do not see it, take care not to negate cause and effect. Zhenjing said:
"When Danxia burned the wooden Buddha, the temple master’s beard and eyebrows fell off. He raised his staff and said, "This is no wooden Buddha," then threw it down and said, "Who dares to burn you?
If you intend to act, your beard and eyebrows will fall; if you do not intend, how will it be? [Zhenjing] called out loudly, "Attendant, pick it up!"
He picked up his staff. Tiantong Hua said, "People say the abbot gave rise to doubt, which led to this calamity;
they do not realize that the abbot has bought iron and obtained gold—a truly magnificent fortune. A monk asked Zhi Xuan, "Why have the abbot’s beard and eyebrows fallen out?"
Zhizhi said, "One person transmits what is false; ten thousand people transmit what is true. [The monk] said, "If that is so, then one does not fall [into error].
Zhizhi said, "A double case. [The monk] said, "I do not understand. He requested further instruction. Zhizhi said, "Jing, Yuan, Qian, and Ji—monks with brushes stuck in their hair.
A monk asked Zhaozhou, "What is the meaning of the West? The Master said, "The cypress tree in the courtyard. [The monk] said, "Do not take it..."
When the situation appeared to be that of a person, the Master said, "I do not take the situation to be a person.
A monk asked, "What is the meaning of the coming from the West? The Master replied, "The cypress tree in the courtyard. Fayan asked Guangxiao, "Have you heard the 'Cypress Tree' story of Zhaozhou?
He replied, "No. Fayan said, "Everyone says there is such a saying; why do you say there is none? He replied, "My late master truly had no such words. Do not slander him. Jing... (text breaks off)
Shan said: "If you say there is a path, you miss Jue Tiezui; if you say there is no path, you miss Fayen.
If you say it does not involve either side, you miss Zhaozhou. Even if you do none of these things, there is still another way to break through."
"Entering hell is like being struck by an arrow. "Ultimately, how is it? Holding up his whisk, he said, "Do you understand? He let out a shout.

A guest asked Xuedou, "Jueyan said that Zhaozhou did not have these words; why did your eyes approve of them? Xian said, "In the Gate of the Patriarchs, is there ever a fixed rule for suppression or exaltation?
Han Da-bei smiled inwardly and departed. Xian asked him, "Han, what were you laughing at? He replied, "I was laughing at Guest Master Yan."
Not yet correct. The verse says: A single hare lies across the ancient road; A blue hawk sees it and seizes it instantly. Later hunters’ dogs lack spiritual nature;
They vainly search for it at the old spot where the withered stump stood. This clarifies the formation of friendship.
Later, Xian sang the Way at Xuedou. He cited a question asked of Yunmen: "When the tree is stripped of its leaves, what then? Yunmen said: "The body reveals the gold."
"Wind. Yunmen answered this monk: was it as a response? Or was it as an explanation? The Senior Monk Zong said, "Wait until this old man has attained realization, and then I will speak.
Xian looked at him in surprise and said, "Is this not Han Daba? [Zong] replied, "The old man has had a sudden flash of insight.
Because of this, Xian requested to ascend the seat and preach the Dharma. Zhaozhou asked a monk, "Have you ever been here before? The monk said, "I have. The Master [said], "..."
"Go drink tea," he said. Again, he asked a monk, "Have you been here before? The monk replied, "No. The Master said, "Go drink tea.
The head monk asked, "Why do you always tell them to go drink tea? The Master called to the head monk; when the head monk responded, the Master said, "Go drink tea.
Muzhou asked a monk, "What is the meaning behind Zhaozhou telling him to drink tea? The monk said, "It is merely a provisional expedient for the occasion. Muzhou said, "Zhao..."
"The Prefecture has been hit by you with a ladle of dung! [Baizhang] struck him. Muzhou asked the śrāmaṇera, "You, sir!
The śrāmaṇera bowed. Muzhou also struck him. A monk asked the śrāmaṇera, "Why did he strike you? He replied, "It was not my teacher who did not strike me. Xuedou said:
"This monk used a ladle of dung to wipe away these two ancient Buddhas. If you can discern this, not only will the two prefectures of Zhao and Mu be cleared of their stains."
It is truly a matter of regret that even Cuiyan and the venerable elders of the world could not discern this; they have been splashing people about everywhere until now.
A monk asked, "Does a dog have Buddha-nature? Zhaozhou said, "No. The monk asked, "Since all sentient beings possess Buddha-nature, why does a dog not?
Zhaozhou said, "It has its karmic consciousness. Furthermore, another monk asked, "Does a dog have Buddha-nature?"... [text ends]
Xing said, "There is none. Zhao said, "There is. [The monk] asked, "If there is one, why enter this skin bag? Zhao said, "Knowing it, yet committing the offense.
A monk asked, "Where does the road to Mount Tai lead? The old woman said, "Go straight on. When the monk left, the old woman said, "What a fine monk, yet he goes off like that.
Later, someone reported this to Zhaozhou. Zhaozhou said, "Wait, I shall go and investigate him myself."
He then asked, "Where does the road to Mount Tai go? The woman said, "Go straight ahead. Baizhang immediately went on his way.
The woman said, "What a fine monk, yet he goes away like that. Baizhang said to the monk, "The woman of Mount Tai has seen through you.
Master Zeng asked Xuedou, "When you were discussing the ultimate point with Old Qing, was there a moment when you saw through him? Xuedou said:
Qingdao said, "What is this 'going along'? Zeng said, "And so you go on like this. Dou said, "Old Qingdao, set that aside for a moment;
do you know that no monk in the world can escape this old woman’s circle? Zeng said, "There is another way here."
If Zhaozhou had not exposed the old woman, she would have suffered a lifelong injustice. Dou said, "He exposed her.
Xuanjue said, "Zhaozhou went away saying the same thing; where was the exposure?
Furthermore, it was not only the old woman who was exposed by Zhaozhou, but this monk as well. A monk asked, "All phenomena return to the One; to what does the One return? Zhaozhou—
The Governor said, "When I was in Qingzhou, I made a garment of plain cloth that weighed seven *jin*. Xuedou’s verse comments:
"Having encountered the ancient master in debate, Who knows the weight of the seven-*jin* robe? Now it is cast into West Lake; To whom shall this cool breeze be delivered?
A monk asked, "What is the Dharma-body? Jia Shan replied, "The Way of the Dharma is formless."
Question: "What is the Dharma-eye? Answer: "The Dharma-eye is without flaw. Daowu could not help but laugh and said, "The Master has no teacher yet.
He then urged him to go to Shipin (Boatman) at Huating. As soon as Shipin saw him, he asked, "In what monastery do you reside?
Jia replied, "I do not reside in a monastery; if I were to reside, I would not be like this. Shipin said, "Not being like this—what are you like?"
"What is it? Jia said. "It is not the dharma before one's eyes. Chuan said, "Where did you learn that? Jia said, "It is not something reached by the ears or the eyes.
Chuan said, "A single phrase that fits the head is a tethering stake for ten thousand kalpas. Chuan asked again, "The line hangs down a thousand feet; the intent lies in the deep pool.
It is three inches away from the hook—why do you not speak? As Jia was about to open his mouth, he was struck.

Once, when Yangshan was struck into the water by a single blow from a pole, as soon as he climbed back onto the boat, he prepared to speak; the boatman struck him again. Yangshan attained great enlightenment and nodded his head three times.
The boatman said: "The line on the tip of the pole is for you to handle as you wish; yet, not disturbing the clear waves, its meaning is naturally distinct.

Yangshan asked: "How is it to cast the line and throw the hook? The boatman said: "The thread hangs in the green water, floating with the intent of both existence and non-existence. Yangshan said: [I understand].

The words carry the profound mystery yet leave no path; the tongue speaks, yet speaks not. Nanquan said, "I have fished through the waves of the river until at last I encountered the golden-scaled fish.
Yajue covered his ears. Nanquan said, "So it is, so it is. He further instructed him, saying, "In the future, you must vanish from where there is a place to hide the body;
do not hide the body where there is no trace to be found. While I was at Yaoshan, I clarified nothing other than this matter. Yajue.
As he was departing, he looked back repeatedly. The boatman raised his oar and said, "You seem to think there is something else. Thereupon, he overturned the boat and vanished into the water.
Later, Daowu again sent a monk to ask, "What is the Dharma-body? He replied, "The Dharma-body has no form. The monk asked again, "What is the Dharma-eye?
Jia replied, "The Dharma-eye has no flaw. When the monk reported this to Daowu, Daowu said, "This fellow, this time..."
Fangche said: "When Master Furong Kai asked, 'What is the Dharmakāya? the sheep lay down on dry ground. When he asked, 'What is the Dharma-eye?
the donkey urinated in a damp place. When he further asked, 'What is the Dharmakāya? [the answer was] 'Buying a hat to fit the head. When he asked, 'What is the Dharma-eye?
[the answer was] 'Ditches, pits, mounds, and hills. Jiangshan’s training was not yet clear; he remained confined within the domestic gate."
It cannot be so. If this old monk did not manifest it directly before you, later students would find it difficult to know where to turn.
I urge you: do not seek the Truth; you must only cease your views. When all views cease, the mirror of wisdom becomes brilliantly clear.

Do you understand? There is fire within the pearl; you must believe this. Do not go to the edge of the sky to ask for the sun. When Lingyun saw peach blossoms, he attained enlightenment. His verse says:

"For thirty years I have been a seeker of the sword; / How many times have fallen leaves sprouted again? / Since the moment I first beheld the peach blossoms, / To this very day, I have had no further doubts.
Miaoshan instructed him, saying: "Awakening through conditions leads to realization; once attained, it shall never be lost."
Xuansha held up [the staff] and said, "It is exactly so, most exactly so; yet I dare guarantee that you, elder brother, have not yet reached the ultimate.
Xuansha asked Dizang, "How do you understand this? Dizang said, "If it were not Guichen, he would have run all the people in the world to death. Miaoxi said:
"When one family has business, a hundred families are busy. A verse on this saying goes: "The ghost-gate is shattered;
the sun is at its zenith. An arrow hits the red heart; not an inch of earth remains. Yian once requested instruction from the Elder Huazang.
The answer is: It is Śākyamuni himself, yet he has not yet reached the ultimate. Miaoshan asked Yangshan, "Where have you come from?
Yangshan replied, "From the fields. Miaoshan asked, "How many people were there? Yangshan thrust his spade into the ground and stood with hands folded.

Miaoshan said, "Today on South Mountain, there are many people cutting thatch. Yangshan pulled out his spade and immediately departed. Xuansha said, "If I had seen him, I would have stepped right on top of him."
The Spade. A monk asked, "What is the meaning of planting the spade? Jingqing said, "A dog bites a royal pardon; the feudal lords clear the way.
[The monk] asked, "What about being trampled by the sand? He replied, "There is nothing one can do about the boat; break the scoop. Again he asked, "What about cutting the thatch at Nanshan?
Jingqing said, "Li Jing, the Third Elder, has long been experienced in the ranks of battle. Yunju Xi said, "Now tell me, what did Jingqing mean?"

This single judgment is clear as to whether one has attained it or not. A monk asked Mingzhao, "The ancients' intent lay in the place where the spade was thrust in, or in the place where the hands were crossed.
Mingzhao called to the monk; the monk responded. Mingzhao said, "Have you ever dreamed of Yangshan?
Xiangyan said, "Discussing this matter is like a person climbing a tree, with a branch in his mouth, his feet not treading on branches, and his hands not grasping branches. Suddenly, there is—"
When someone asked about the meaning of the Westward Journey, [Yunmen] did not answer. To fail to answer is to contradict what was asked;
to answer another person is to lose one's body and life. At such a time, what would you do? Houtou Zhaoyin said, "I do not ask about when he is on the tree;
please speak before he has climbed the tree. Yanyuan laughed heartily. Xuedou said, "To speak while on the tree is easy; to speak while under the tree is difficult. I, the old monk, will climb up."
It is like a tree. I have come to pose a question. Yuanwu said: "One who possesses the eye of the Xiang lineage does not form interpretations based on 'yes' or 'no.
Before a word is even raised, they already know where it falls. If you hesitate or deliberate, you will miss it face-to-face. Or, one does not fall into either extreme."
"It is neither right nor wrong. How, then, can one see where the ancients have arrived? A monk went to Shishuang and cited Dongshan’s words:
"Brothers, whether you go east or west, you must go to a place ten thousand *li* away where there is not a single blade of grass.
After a long silence, he asked, "As for that place ten thousand *li* away where there is not a single blade of grass—how does one go there? Shishuang said, "Why do you not..."
"The Way lies just outside the gate, yet it is overgrown with weeds. Dongwen said, "Is there truly an ancient Buddha in Liuyang?
Tanyang Yan replied, "Even if one does not step out the gate directly, the weeds still stretch far and wide. He then asked, "Tell me, how should one practice?
After a long silence, he said, "Do not linger by the green herbs on the cold crag; sitting amidst white clouds is ultimately not the ultimate state. Yuantong Shan said, "And furthermore—"
Regarding the phrase "at the heels of the Way," how would you respond? If you say, "Ten thousand miles, not an inch of grass," I allow that you have seen Dongshan.
If you say, "Stepping out the door is already grass," I allow that you have seen Shishuang.
If you say, "Even without stepping out, it is a vast expanse of grass," I allow that you have seen Taiyang. If you cannot say anything at all, I allow that you have visited Yansheng. Why is this so?

On what principle do you speak thus? Xinghua gave a shout. Dajue struck him. Xinghua shouted again. Dajue struck him again. The following day, Dajue said:
"I have a direct doubt regarding those two shouts you gave yesterday. When I shouted, Huairang hit me; when I shouted again, Huairang hit me once more.
I said, 'I studied the "Guest and Host" phrase under Sanxing, yet I have been utterly defeated by him. I pray he will grant me a Dharma-gate of peace and ease.
Huairang said, 'This fellow has come here to suffer defeat. Take off your patched robe and receive a severe beating!'"
He gave him a beating. This illustrates the principle behind Linji receiving the staff. Xinghua said to Kebin, "Before long, you will become a leader of the assembly.
Kebin replied, "I will not enter this community. Xinghua asked, "Do you refuse to enter because you understand, or because you do not understand?
Kebin replied, "In either case, I will not. Xinghua then struck him, saying, "Venerable Abbot Kebin, you have lost the battle for the Dharma!"
"A fine of five *guan* shall be imposed, and a single meal shall be provided. On the following day, he said again, "Kebin shall not eat this meal; he is expelled from the monastery.
Yunju Shun remarked, "In a great furnace, refined gold does not change its color. Xinghua’s command was strict, yet it was not difficult for Kebin to uphold.

Guang also struck his meditation mat once. Jing said, "He strikes, you strike too. Guang attained great enlightenment. Jing then spoke in verse:
"A man of worth should sever [delusion] himself; Xinghua is a thoroughgoing man for the sake of others. Henceforth, let his own eyes open by themselves;
bound with a staff and fined, he is driven out of the monastery. Luopo went to visit Jia Shan. He stood with hands joined in *añjali*. Jia Shan said, "The rooster..."
Xiqi said, "The phoenix nests; those who are not of its kind must depart. Guoqing Luo said, "I have come from afar to follow the wind of your teaching;
I beg the Master for a single meeting. Xiqi said, "Before my eyes there is no *śrāmaṇera*; here there is no old monk. Luo then gave a shout. Xiqi said, "Stop, stop!
Clouds and moon are the same; streams and mountains are each different. To cut off the tongues of all people under heaven is certainly possible, but how can you make them tongueless?"
Renshan understood the words, while Luozhu stood there lost in thought. Jia immediately struck him; from this, Luozhu took the teaching to heart.

One day he asked, "When the morning sun has already risen and the night moon has not yet appeared, what is it like? Jia replied, "The dragon carries a pearl in its mouth; the swimming fish do not look back. Luozhu attained great enlightenment.
When Xuefeng was serving as the head cook, the meal was late. Deshan went down to the Dharma Hall with his alms bowl. Xuefeng said, "The bell has not yet rung."
Before the drum had even sounded, Deshan set out with his alms bowl toward an unknown destination. Deshan then returned directly to the abbot’s quarters.

Feng reported this to Yantou, who said, "Great as Master Deshan may be, he has not yet realized the final word. When Deshan heard this, he called for Yantou and asked, "Why do you refuse to acknowledge me?

Yantou secretly revealed his intention, whereupon Deshan desisted. The following day, when Deshan ascended the hall, it was unlike anything he had done before. Yantou went to the monks' hall and clapped his hands.
Master Zhaozhou said with a laugh, "I am glad that this old fellow understands the final word. Hereafter, no one will be able to do anything with him.

Nevertheless, he shall live for only three years. Indeed, Deshan died after three years. Master Dahui Zonggao of Mount Jing composed this verse: "A single blow of the 'poisoned drum'—all who hear it perish;
Though they stand right in its midst, none at all know it. An eighty-year-old grandfather entering the examination hall— Truly, this is no joke!"
While a young child was playing, a monk arrived. Xuefeng leaned on the gate of the hermitage with his hand and, stepping out, asked, "What is this?
The monk also said, "What is this? Xuefeng lowered his head and returned to the hermitage. When the monk took his leave and went to Yantou, he recounted the previous conversation.
Yantou asked, "What did he say? [The monk] replied, "He was speechless. Yantou said, "At that moment, I regretted not telling him: 'The final word.'"
[The Master] said: "If you were to speak toward the Way, no one could do anything about Old Xue. When the monk reached the end of summer, he requested further instruction on the previous dialogue.
Yankou said: "Why did you not ask sooner? The monk replied: "I did not dare to be casual. Yankou said: "Although Xuefeng was born of the same lineage as I, he does not die of the same lineage as I.
If you wish to recognize the final word, it is simply this. Xuedou’s verse says: "The final word... [toward].
You say: "At the moment when light and darkness are paired, those of the same root are born and know one another; those of different roots die and are utterly severed. Utterly severed!
Yellow-headed and blue-eyed, you must discern the difference. North, south, east, and west—go and return!"
Deep in the night, they gazed together at the snow upon a thousand crags. A monk asked Jìngshān Gǎo, "Why did he lower his head and return to his hut?

Gǎo replied, "It would leave the whole world in doubt. Again, the monk asked about Yàntóu’s "final word. Gǎo said, "If you do not sleep in the same bed, how can you know there is a hole in the bottom of the quilt?
Again, the monk asked, "Born of the same lineage, yet dying of different lineages. Gǎo said, "To kill a person, one must truly kill."
The Human Blade: To truly enliven a person, one must possess the sword that enlivens people. Baofu asked, "In this way, in this way; not in this way, not in this way—how is it?
Luoshan called out to Baofu. Baofu responded, "Yes. Luoshan said, "Both are bright, yet both are dark. Later, Baofu asked, "What is meant by 'both are bright, yet both are dark'?
He replied, "Born together, they die together. Separately, another monk asked [the same question]. [Luoshan] replied, "Born together, they die together."
Fú asked, "What is it like when one is born together and dies together? Fú replied, "Both should shut their mouths like dogs.
The monk said, "Master, please close your mouth and eat your rice. That monk then asked Luoshan, "What is it like when one is born together and dies together?"
Luoshan said, "It is like a cow without horns. When asked, "What is it like when they are born together but do not die together? he replied, "It is like a tiger wearing horns.
When asked of Dongshan, "If a snake swallows a frog, should one save it or not?
Dongshan said, "If you save it, both eyes will fail to see; if you do not save it, its form and shadow will not be manifest. Huanji said, "The Inspector of Lianzhou asked Mazu: [and so forth].
"Is it right to eat meat and drink wine? Or is it not? The Patriarch said, "To eat is the official’s emolument; to abstain is the official’s blessing.
Someone asked Master Guoyi, "At a roadside inn, a sheep was being slaughtered. One person tried to save it, while another did not. Are their karmic retributions for sin and merit different?"
Guo said: "The savior is compassion; the non-savior is liberation. These three venerable elders—one was struck by thunder and swept away by lightning, yet fell into the leakage of views;
one shone like a pearl and was as smooth as jade, yet fell into the leakage of emotion;

one was as lofty as a mountain and as deep as water, yet fell into the leakage of words. If you can discern them, you have eyes but are as if blind; if you cannot discern them," [you are likewise blind].
There are those who have mouths but are as if mute. Others may say, "It emerged whole and complete, without the slightest discrepancy," yet they beat their breasts and weep bitterly day after day.
Yunmen asked Dongshan Chuyu, "Where have you recently departed from? He replied, "Chadu. Yunmen asked, "Where were you during the summer retreat?
He replied, "Baoci in Hunan. Yunmen asked, "When did you leave there? He replied, "The twenty-fifth of the sixth month. Yunmen said:
"I grant you three blows of the staff. On the following day, Dayu asked, "Where does the fault lie? Yunmen said, "You rice-bag! You go off to Jiangxi and Hunan acting just like this.
At these words, Dayu attained great enlightenment and said, "In the future, I shall go to places where there is no human habitation and not store even a single grain of rice.
I will receive those who come and go, and for them all, I will pull out their nails and extract their wedges. I will strip off their cloth robes and teach them."
"Be a monk of non-action," he said. [The monk] replied, "Your body is as large as a coconut, yet you open such a wide mouth.

When [the monk] first prostrated, Yuanwu said, "It is precisely because Yunmen’s words are excellent that you can discard your intellectual interpretations and immediately realize Dongshan’s point of awakening.
It is like Linji, who, when confronted by Dayu, discarded his emotional views and thereby attained thorough realization. Later, a monk asked:
"What is the Buddha? he asked, and immediately replied, "Three pounds of flax. Observe where this was arrived at through deliberate arrangement;
in the Gate of the Patriarchs, one sees it upon a single glance. Although he thus punctures the fundamental principle (*mūla*), his intent nonetheless lies in the state before birth.
For those with clear eyes, there is no fixed nest or trap. Thus Yantou said: "If we speak of battle, everyone stands at the point of turning."

If you look once before it has even been excreted, you will see it at once; it is vast and open, appearing as a single path. A clever person who encounters a point of doubt will understand it instantly upon a single glance.
Wuzu Yan said: "It is like an ox passing through a window frame: its head, horns, and four hooves all pass through."
For what reason does the tail not pass through? Gao Feng Miao’s verse says: "Carelessly releasing this ox, its horns and head clearly displayed—show it to whom?
If you understand it by the tip of the tail, the hawks of Silla have long since passed away."
Xueyan cited the case where Emperor Wu of Liang asked the First Patriarch, "What is the primary meaning of the holy truth?

The Patriarch replied, "Vast emptiness; there is no saint. The Emperor said, "Who is it that stands before me? He replied, "I do not know. The Emperor did not attain realization. Later, when the Patriarch had gone to Wei, Emperor Wu asked Master Zhi about him.
Zhi asked, "Does Your Majesty recognize this man? The Emperor said, "I do not recognize him. Zhi said, "This is Guanyin Bodhisattva."
Shi transmitted the Buddha’s mind-seal to the Emperor, who said, "I shall dispatch an envoy to summon him. Zhi replied, "Do not speak of Your Majesty;

even if the entire nation were to pursue him, he would not return. The First Patriarch and Emperor Wu pressed each other back and forth like two mirrors reflecting one another, with no space between them even for a hair.
Unprovoked, Zhigong applied colorful paint to the bright mirror, turning empty space into a veil of flaws and obscurations.
Emperor Wu asked about the primary principle (*paramārtha*). The teachings speak of two truths: the conventional and the ultimate;
the primary principle is precisely the ultimate truth. [The Master] replied, "Vastly empty, there is no sage. Now tell me: was this a response spoken for Emperor Wu, or was it his own words?
Ultimately, what is the meaning of "vastly empty, there is no sage"? What does the primary principle take as its fundamental reliance? Brothers, at this point you must truly exert your eyes.
Only through careful discernment can this be grasped. Often it is thought that Huineng was thoroughly deceived by Huiming right before his eyes;
yet one fails to realize that Huineng was a master king who had no need for even a single word from him.
He immediately asked, "Who is facing me?"—a truly intimate phrase, my brother. When Huiming reached this point, he could not help but reveal his true nature.
When he came, the Master said, "I do not recognize you. Wu did not harmonize with this; it was as if a vast iron net had been cast across the heavens.
Later, he asked Master Zhi about it, wishing for these words to spread widely. Zhi asked, "Does Your Majesty recognize this man? [The Emperor replied,] "His arm does not bend outward.
Zhi said, "I do not recognize him. [The Emperor said,] "Damo has not yet departed. Zhi said, "This is the transmission of Guanyin."
The Master said, "The Buddha-mind school is like a harmonious sound; it is best to set it aside for a moment. Wuzu said, "One should dispatch an envoy with an imperial decree;
one must be able to grant and to take away, to kill and to give life. Guizong said, "If the entire nation were to leave, they would not return. If they did return, what would they be fit for?"

This is the very first *huatou* (critical phrase) under the gate of the Patriarchs. As for those who have offered verses or picked it up, there have been countless numbers throughout the past and present;
yet none have failed to say that Wuzhuo missed the mark. Truly, it is said that "the knife and the sword look alike. With one arrow, one usually strikes down a single bird;
if one adds another arrow, one has already let the other go. Return directly to sit before the peak of Shaoshi. Let the Prince of Liang not speak further.
"Go further to summon him. This is Baiyun’s verse on the line "A falcon falls; the verse is vast and empty, without a sage. To add an arrow is to fail to recognize this.
Such conceptual calculations of intellectual consciousness—what end of the Master do you seek?
The final two lines are merely ordinary, colloquial speech. Generally, the language of the Chan school does not speak of essence, but speaks of function; it does not speak of phenomena.

He then explains the principle: "If one has personally seen the white clouds in the two preceding lines, only then will one know that in a single phrase there is the whole body and in a single phrase there is the whole function;

thus both principle and phenomenon are complete. The white clouds and the Patriarch were like emperors meeting at the heart of the Yangtze River, yet they encountered each other atop the Phoenix Terrace.
Xuedou’s verse says: "The Holy Truth is vast and open; how can it be discerned? Facing me..."
"Who is it? he asked, and [the other] replied, "I do not know. These four lines were completed in a single verse because his talent was broad. Furthermore, he added a footnote:
"Because of this, crossing the river in secret—how can one avoid the thorns that grow? These two lines occupy so much ground. The people of the whole land pursue him, but he does not return;
for ten thousand ages, they can only remember him in vain. Do not remember him! The pure breeze..."
What limit can there be to the whole earth? The essential point is to penetrate this one phrase; if you can do so, I will allow you to pass through the seventeen hundred cases.
But tell me, where does it land? Is there a patriarch here? Call him over and let him wash the old monk’s feet.
Baoning Yong’s Verse: Refined until glowing red, struck with a single hammer-blow; Countless sparks fly about on all sides.
A perfect, ten-part diamond— Laid out before the gate, to whom shall it be sold? These four lines leave you no place to take a bite;
there is no room for calculation. Tell me, upon whose side does this fall: that of Bodhidharma, Emperor Wu, or Master Zhi? You must...
This was first attained by Heshan. Nan also has a verse: "The ten-thousand-mile road from the West is long and winding; The mirror of wisdom faces the window—no shadow can escape it.
When the waves of the four seas are stilled, the dragon sleeps soundly; When the clouds of the nine heavens are clear, the crane flies high. Yuanwu said: "Emperor Wu did not recognize [Bodhidharma].
Is what he said the same as or different from what Bodhidharma spoke? Many people mistakenly understand Bodhidharma’s response."
"His meditation. 'Mu' is a cognition that cognizes characteristics; it has nothing to do with it.
When Master Zhì asked this, why did he not strike him dead with a single blow to avoid such muddled confusion? Xueyan cited Mazu’s "sitting in meditation": "A stagnant pond does not harbor dragons.
Nanyang Huizhong asked, "What are you seeking?"—this is "beating the grass to startle the snake. Mazu replied, "I am seeking to become a Buddha"—his deluded thoughts were no small matter.

Xiangruang took the brick and began to grind it. Mazu said, "What are you doing? Xiangruang replied, "I am grinding it into a mirror. Mazu said, "The brick will never become a mirror. Xiangruang said, "If grinding a brick cannot produce a mirror, how can sitting in meditation bring one to Buddhahood? Mazu asked, "How then? [In this exchange, Xiangruang’s action of grinding the brick represents the futile effort of seeking enlightenment through mere physical discipline;

Mazu’s response points to the necessity of realizing one's inherent nature. Xiangruang said, "Grinding a brick does not make a mirror; sitting in meditation does not make a Buddha. Mazu asked, "How then? Xiangruang replied, "It reveals the face of one's original nature. Mazu then asked, "How so? (Or: "What is it? *Note: The phrase "Chuisi qianchi" (垂絲千尺) means "a thousand feet of dangling line," suggesting a state of total openness and readiness to respond.

"Zaoshenqianchi" (上鉤了也) means "he has already taken the hook," indicating that the student has been caught by the master's teaching. "Yizai shentan" (意在深潭) means "the intent lies in the deep pool," signifying that the true meaning resides in the profound depths of reality. "Luchu benlai mian" (露出本來面) means "revealing the face of the original nature."*
This is precisely it: seizing the throat. Letting Yuan let out a cry, he said, "The ox will not pull the cart. [Baizhang] struck the cart; was it the cart he struck, or the ox?

He shouted, "If you can take responsibility for this shout, then whether it be striking the ox or striking the cart, Master Yuan’s brick in his hand will shatter into a hundred pieces, until its cold radiance blazes forth, piercing through mountains and rivers. Yuan then said, "You have studied..."
Sitting in meditation. Meditation is neither sitting nor lying down; the Buddha, too, is not a fixed form. Within the dharma of non-abiding, one should neither grasp nor reject.
If you study by imitating the seated Buddha, this is precisely killing the Buddha. Failing to penetrate this principle, the horse hears it as if drinking clarified butter (amṛta).

The ancients had sharp faculties; with a single nudge, they were transformed. Why do people today not reflect upon whether one is striking the ox or striking the cart? Ultimately, what is the intention behind this?
"How is it? You should know that this is the diamond circle and the thorn-bush of the *liji* fruit. Try to chew upon it;
only when you casually bite into it will you realize that polishing a brick truly results in a mirror. Sitting in meditation will never produce a Buddha. The verse says:
"When all dharmas are forgotten and a hundred thoughts turn to ash, One casually seizes the nose and drags one back. The mirror-light shines forth, bright as the sun, Until one attains..."
The mind and eyes of the man of wood have opened. Regarding Xueyan’s citation of Baizhang’s second visit to Mazu: On this day, I respectfully wish you ten thousand blessings.
Mazu held up his whisk and said, "Use it right here; do not use it apart from here. To do so is to create artificial distinctions.

Mazu hung the whisk back in its original place. As always, in the early spring, it is still cold. Mazu then asked, "After this, with what will you provide for others? It is not permissible [to answer].
There is yet another point. Baizhang also held up his whisk. A fine son never uses his father’s money. Mazu said, "The very function is itself the departure from that function;
there is not the slightest difference. Baizhang hung the whisk back in its original place. "In total, one cannot depart from this. Mazu let out a thunderous shout. "A disgraceful manner!
Baizhang attained great enlightenment, to the extent that he was deaf for three days. Is it truly so? Often...

Upon shouting "Katsu!", he attained great enlightenment. He did not realize that there is no genuine *arura* (myrrh) and no counterfeit gold. The old monks of past and present have failed to distinguish blue from yellow;
only Xuedou has managed to get the better of them slightly. He said: "Refined gold from a great furnace should not change its color.

Regarding this, Fengyang’s verse says: "Once, for no particular reason, I attended before my teacher; the teacher pointed to something hanging on the corner of the rope-cot. I picked it up and set it down, then returned."
Established upon its own ground, this distinct single shout has been transmitted to this day. To follow the vermilion and fill in the ink is not the work of a master hand.
Zhenjing’s verse says: "Guest sentiments turn with every step one takes; Though there is great majestic light, it cannot be seen.
Suddenly, a shout deafens both ears; Nata’s eyes open, and Huangbo’s face appears. A person of great power turns away from speech and silence. —Miaoxi.
Verse: Under the hooves of the colt, the family tradition is lost; from this day forth, news shall pass through the four seas.

To pluck the moon from amidst a mass of fierce flames—lofty and solitary, he sits atop the Great Hero’s Peak. There is no lack of principle to be explained, yet if you wish to see Mazu and Baizhang, they remain far away.
Brothers, if you would take up this matter, it is like a rushing torrent or a swift flame: before you can blink, the sword has already gone.
When the Master [Zhaozhou] first saw the staff raised, he immediately broke it into two pieces; that was still slightly better.

To pointlessly ask whether it is used in conjunction with or apart from [the staff], you have already placed the nose-rope in his hands. You were then dragged along by him until he let out a thunderous shout, at which point you claimed to have attained great enlightenment and were deaf for three days.
How deeply shameful! Do you know shame? This mountain monk, seeing injustice on the road, shall provide [retribution].
A single verse: A shout strikes the head like a bolt of lightning; even those who hear it spoken lose their spirits in darkness. Looking at it, how could it merely deafen one for three days?
It remains until this very day, darkening the seas and mountains. Xueyan said: "The mountains are green and the waters are blue; day is bright and night is dark.
All are the light of the Treasury of the True Dharma-Eye, manifest in every instance, unchanging throughout ten thousand kalpas. Yet Linji...
"The Way is extinguished at the side of the blind donkey. Is this not a perverse statement? It is a pity that Sansheng did not cut it off for him.
[Jiashan] replied, "How would I dare extinguish it? This supports [Sansheng] and adds a cup to Jiashan’s drunkenness. When asked, "What do you say? Sansheng also gave a shout;
it was simply three hours too late, which allowed Jiashan to seize the Great Sword and bring it to its full extent.
The followers of the School of the Ground (Dilun) have remained tongue-tied and speechless until now. This mountain monk, seeing injustice on the road, intended to clear away their errors for them.
Yet, as Jue was about to pass away, he had the potential to enter hell. After my passing, you must not extinguish the True Eye.

Sheng said, "How would I dare extinguish it? [Jue replied,] "It has already been swept away. Jue said, "If someone suddenly asks me, what shall I say? [Sheng said,] "Wait for the question, then answer."
The Holy One (Linji) gave a shout and said, "What a fuss! Who would have known that the Eye of the True Dharma would perish upon a blind donkey?
[Pointing behind Linji’s head, he continued: "You all—do you see Linji here? If you see him, the Eye of the True Dharma perishes upon the blind donkey;
if you do not see him, the Eye of the True Dharma perishes upon the blind donkey. Now tell me, where does the error lie?"
"Where is it? Baoning Yong’s verse says: "Leaving the gate, he took my hand and cautioned me again and again. Often enough, matters arise from such instructions.
The road is long and the night is deep; do not carry a torch. Everyone should blow it out and walk in the dark.

Now, as for the line "the road is long and the night is deep," this verse refers to [the words] "extinguish them before the blind donkey. Do not slander Baoning! Fojian’s verse says: "Extinguish them before the blind donkey."

He extinguished the Eye of the True Dharma, yet produced a lineage that filled the Great Tang. One must believe that amidst the vast, distant mists and waves, there is clearly another way to deliberate.
But tell me, what is it they deliberate upon? I too have a verse: "Killing and enlivening, acting with total freedom;
Casting off one's hands at the precipice to seek out an enemy. The blind donkey extinguishes the Eye of the True Dharma; A cold light pierces the stars."

The light was not gathered at night. Yunyan cited Nan-yuan’s saying: “The various quarters possess only the eye of the simultaneous pecking and hatching, but they do not possess the function of the simultaneous pecking and hatching.
Such talk not only brings humiliation upon the various quarters, but it also plays with the sons and daughters of other houses.
When it is exactly thus, to call it the “simultaneous function” is correct; to call it the “simultaneous [eye]” is also correct.
